items.title: 2.1 Atomic number, proton number and nucleon number; identity of an element

source_refs.note: Topic 2.1, printed pages 23-24: atomic number, nucleon number, N = A - Z, ions and Table 2.1. The chapter's learning outcomes are interleaved in the print and not reproduced.

blocks.text: In 1913 Moseley observed that when different elements were bombarded with cathode rays, X-rays of characteristic frequencies were produced, and that the square root of the frequency of the X-rays was directly proportional to the atomic number Z of the element. He concluded that this number, the atomic number Z, is a fundamental property of an element. It is also called the proton number. The number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus together is the nucleon number A, also called the mass number, and the two are related by A = Z + N. An atom of an element X with atomic number Z and mass number A is written with A above and Z below the symbol, for example Al-27 with Z = 13. The number of neutrons is N = A - Z.

For Al-27: atomic (proton) number Z = 13, mass (nucleon) number A = 27, so N = 27 - 13 = 14. The electrons, protons and neutrons of an ion follow in the same way. When the Al-27 atom loses three electrons to form Al3+ it has 13 protons, 14 neutrons and 13 - 3 = 10 electrons. When a chlorine atom gains an electron to form Cl- it has 17 protons, 18 neutrons and 17 + 1 = 18 electrons. The atomic number and the proton number therefore represent the same concept.
